acceptedReports.priceScope: Whole-organization cost against only workforce earnings gains from a randomized trial; other programs unquantified; income-only welfare comparison, not a verified marginal gift offer

what: St. Nicks Alliance is a Brooklyn community organization that runs job training, affordable housing, youth programs and elder care.

Its workforce programs train adults and young people for certifications in construction, HVAC, environmental remediation, building maintenance and healthcare, and it reports placing over 1,000 people a year in jobs or further education.
This in-depth review charges the whole organization’s cost against only the earnings gains its environmental-remediation training produced in a randomized trial.
strengths: In MDRC’s randomized WorkAdvance trial of about 480 applicants, St. Nicks’ training raised average earnings by 32% in year 10 and the share earning $45,000 or more by 7 points.
It is the only one of the four WorkAdvance providers with a significant earnings effect ten years after enrollment.
Its other services (housing, youth and elder care) add value we do not count, so the estimate is conservative.
reservations: Our working estimate is about $5.27M per better life; it counts only workforce earnings while charging the whole budget.
Gains appeared only in years 8 to 10; earlier years showed no significant effect, so the result could be a late fluke.
Today’s workforce programs cover many more trades than the tested environmental-remediation track, so transfer is uncertain.

sections.what: St. Nicks Alliance (St Nicks Alliance Corp, EIN 51-0192170) works in north Brooklyn. Its workforce division offers skills training and certifications in construction, HVAC, environmental remediation, building maintenance, data analytics, financial services and hemodialysis, plus adult education and youth programs such as YouthBuild. The wider organization also develops affordable housing and runs youth, education and elder-care services. A donation supports the whole organization unless restricted.
sections.monitoring: St. Nicks was a WorkAdvance provider in MDRC’s randomized trial: 242 applicants were assigned to its environmental-remediation program and 237 to a control group, with earnings tracked in administrative wage records for ten years. It reports annual placement counts on its website. We did not find program-level costs, enrollments or completion rates; we have not contacted the organization.
sections.qualitative: At three years the trial found no significant earnings effect at St. Nicks, and the seven-year report attributed WorkAdvance’s pooled gains mainly to Per Scholas. By years 8 to 10, however, St. Nicks participants earned more; in year 10 average earnings were 32% higher and 7 percentage points more earned $45,000 or more. Year 10 overlapped the pandemic recovery. A late-emerging effect is plausible for trades with credential ladders, but it rests on one site and a few years.
sections.cost:
Our central estimate is **$5.27M per better life**, using ten healthy-year welfare equivalents. It is an income-only comparison of the workforce benefit alone.

**Cost.** We charge the CY2023 whole-organization expense, $47.7M, to the roughly 1,000 adults and young people it places each year: $47,666 each. This deliberately loads housing, youth and elder-care spending onto the workforce benefit, so it overstates the cost of the training itself.

**Benefit.** We credit a $6,000 average gross gain in years 8–10 (rising to 32% of a $30,000 base in year 10) and half that for five more years, 60% of it as net welfare. We keep 0.5 for transfer to today’s broader programs, 0.85 for displacement and 0.9 for NYC residence.

**Range.** If a restricted gift bore only workforce costs (assumed a quarter of the budget), the estimate is $1.32M per better life. With no persistence after year 10 it is $9.28M per better life; with full transfer, $2.63M per better life. If the late gains do not replicate, there is no credited benefit.
sections.funding: St Nicks Alliance Corp reported CY2023 expenses of $47.7M, up from $41.9M in 2022 and $35.1M in 2021, with $35.7M of contributions and grants and $10.1M of program service revenue. Related entities include St Nicks Alliance Home Care Corp and a community development corporation, which are not included here. We have not seen a costed plan for added workforce trainees.

model.costScope: CY2023 whole-organization expense divided by about 1,000 people placed per year; non-workforce programs charged but not credited.
model.geographicAttribution: Brooklyn participants; 0.9 of earning years in the NYC metro.
model.formula: Price = 10 × cost per placed participant ÷ Σ [0.5 × discounted years × ln(1 + 0.6 × gain ÷ base) × transfer × non-displacement × NYC share]. Health = 0.
model.counterfactual: Randomized control applicants with access to other training and jobs.
model.attribution: A gift is credited with the transferred average late effect per placed participant at whole-organization cost; other services unquantified.
model.uncertainty: Dominated by whether the late single-site gain is real and transfers to current programs, and by the share of cost that is workforce.
model.nativeOutcomes: Annual earnings and share earning $45,000+ over ten years.
